recipe: If you are using a build.rs script together with a cbindgen.toml configuration file, use cbindgen::generate() instead of the Builder interface.
trigger_condition: You want to combine a build.rs script with a cbindgen.toml configuration file.
evidence: If you'd like to use a `build.rs` script with a `cbindgen.toml`, consider using [`cbindgen::generate()`](https://docs.rs/cbindgen/*/cbindgen/fn.generate.html) instead.

recipe: Use a tuple struct instead of an anonymous tuple when defining types that cbindgen needs to generate C/C++ headers for.
trigger_condition: You are defining a type with multiple fields and want cbindgen to emit a full definition rather than a forward declaration.
evidence: cbindgen sadly cannot ever support anonymous tuples `(A, B, ...)`, as there is no way to guarantee their layout. You must use a tuple struct.

recipe: When you need to pass a Rust slice across the FFI boundary, decompose it into a pointer and length, and reconstruct it on the other side using slice::from_raw_parts.
trigger_condition: Your public C API needs to accept or return a Rust slice type.
evidence: In the case of slices you can at least decompose them into a pointer and length, and reconstruct them with `slice::from_raw_parts`.

recipe: Do not use the [u64; 0] trick to over-align a struct; cbindgen does not support it.
trigger_condition: You are trying to control the alignment of a struct by embedding a zero-length array of a larger type.
evidence: Don't use the `[u64; 0]` trick to over-align a struct, we don't support this.

recipe: Use the [defines] section in your cbindgen.toml to specify how cbindgen should map cfg attributes found in your crate to C preprocessor defines.
trigger_condition: Your crate uses cfg attributes (e.g. target_os, feature) and you need cbindgen to wrap platform-specific or feature-gated items in appropriate #ifdef guards.

recipe: Pin cbindgen to a specific version in your Cargo.toml when using the unstable_ir feature flag, because the internal representation is not stable and will change between versions.
trigger_condition: You need to access cbindgen's internal representation (IR) for parsing or code generation purposes.
evidence: If you use this feature, you will need to pin cbindgen to avoid breakages.

recipe: To override global cbindgen.toml settings for a specific type, add inline annotations as doc comments that start with cbindgen: on that type.
trigger_condition: You need to customize the generated header for one specific type without changing the global configuration.
evidence: While output configuration is primarily done through the cbindgen.toml, in some cases you need to manually override your global settings. In those cases you can add inline annotations to your types, which are doc comments that start with `cbindgen:`.
